## Historical audit — S0343

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_189918915/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only chunk 2 is visible; the referenced images are not visible to this audit.

**Goal versus observation:** The requested goal was a camera-matched, editable 3D reconstruction of a single indoor photograph. The student interpreted it as a warehouse aisle; that interpretation and its reported visual comparisons are not independent verification of the photograph (line 21, `model_request`, characters [0,153841)).

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Scene construction | H’s programs created multiple named assets: roof and girders, skylight and grid, fluorescent fixtures, two racks, pallets and cargo. Rack members and goods were grouped as child parts, with approximate placement rather than independently verified physical connections. Colored materials, emission and area lights were configured; no image textures are evident in the code. Camera position, target, lens and roll were parameterized. No articulated human or object pose is evidenced (line 21, `model_request`, [0,153841); lines 23–24, `model_response` and `execute`, [0,11619) and [0,11356)). |
| First two iterations | Both builds and renders reported success. H described the first render as having nearly vertical lights, an overly prominent opposite rack and a dim, misplaced skylight; it then rolled the camera +25°, moved the right rack outward, changed skylight placement and emission, and varied cargo. The second projection table showed several large differences from estimated reference points. These are student observations and numerical projections, not visual or geometric verification by this audit (line 21, `model_request`, [0,153841)). |
| Third revision and exploration | H reported that the second render’s light and rack slopes were reversed, the lower foreground was too empty, and the skylight too low. It changed roll to −25°, extended rack bays, enlarged cargo, added pallet blocks, darkened steel and moved the skylight. The executed program compared +25°, +20° and −25° projections; the selected foreground shelf projected to (−0.094, 0.811), versus estimated (0.12, 0.73), and the skylight corner to (0.447, 0.377), versus (0.59, 0.20). These checks do not establish visibility or correspondence (lines 23–24, [0,11619), [0,11356); line 29, `execution_result`, [0,66302)). |
| Outcome | Step 3 built and rendered with return code 0 and `ok: true`; step 3 was selected. This is **technical execution success**, not established reconstruction success. No final image inspection or formal visual correctness result is visible here (lines 26, 28–30, `build_completed`, `render_completed`, `execution_result`, `select`, respectively [0,1601), [0,1591), [0,66302), [0,59)). |

**Teacher input and adoption:** The visible request contains general reconstruction and projection-check instructions and repeated prompts to compare renders. H demonstrably used landmark tables and made revisions after the feedback prompts. No separately identified teacher diagnosis, proposed update, or receipt of such feedback is visible in this chunk. The third H session had no observed tool calls; Blender execution was performed by the runner afterward (lines 21–24, including line 22 `codex_session` [0,5737)).

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Separating numerical projections from rendered contours is transferable; roll direction and warehouse cargo density are task-specific hypotheses. Whether the final roll, lighting, materials, gaps, overlaps and part contacts actually match the image remains unresolved, as do hidden geometry and any activity in the unseen chunk.
